rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Deck 2 Set Up 3 Player's Turn 4 Supply 5 Attack 6 Game End Deck 7 Infantry 5 Heavy Weapons 3 Special Forces 3 Tanks 3 Artillery 3 Paratroopers 2 Air Strikes Set Up 1) Each player receives 5 unit cards from deck. 2) Each player discards 2 cards to the bottom of their deck and keeps 3. 3) Each player begins with 2 Air Strike cards. Player's Turn 1) Draw 2 cards from your deck (unless no more cards available). 2) Play 2 cards. (For the first player's first turn, only draw 1 and play 1.) When you play an Air Strike, simply remove any opponent's unit from the board. Supply When you play a unit, it must be supplied. A unit is supplied if either: 1) The unit is IN your base. 2) The unit can trace a supply line (through other friendly units) back to your base. (Aside from Paratroopers, you can only place units where the game tells you that you can.) There are two exceptions: a) Special Forces are supplied by diagonally adjacent units. b) Paratroopers can be placed anywhere (other than in opponent's base). They "supply" themselves. Note: A Paratrooper cannot supply your other units unless it has a supply line back to your base. Attack Units can ONLY attack immediately after being placed. Two stipulations: 1) There must be an enemy unit in attack range. 2) The unit you want to attack must also have ANOTHER friendly unit for which the enemy unit is in "Support" range. To say this another way, you must attack an enemy unit with TWO of your units -- the unit you are placing has the enemy in their "Attack" range AND another friendly unit has the enemy within their "Support" range. If you get this wrong and don't have another supporting unit, the unit you place won't be able to attack. The exceptions are Tank and Artillery, which do not need support to kill an enemy in range. (Notice the attack icon on their cards is different, showing a little flame icon.) Game End When a player places a unit in opponent's base, they win the game immediately. If both players have no cards in hand nor in deck, the game ends, and the player with the most units in play wins.

[Rating: 3/10] 2 / 5 - Fair.  Surprising depth here for such a simple and quick game and at heart, that's the appeal here. The apparent military theme is a bit of a shame - it's mirrored in the gameplay not at all beyond the sense that you're gradually "outflanking" an opponent - this is really an abstract.

I think there are many things to admire about this very clean design.  But it's just not my thing. It's too abstract for my tastes, and it doesn't make me feel like I'm fighting a battle. [Rating: 3/10] Way, way abstract with nothing at all to do with WWII units. Could be rethemed with colors or shapes as the abstract game it really is.

[Rating: 3/10] Meh. Games are too short, and the winning play is always obvious. If you are able to establish solid ground and your opponent doesn't have cards to take you out, you can get the win easily. Just never clicked with me. Not a bad filler game when two players are waiting for the rest of the group, though.

[Rating: 3/10] I was hoping for an interesting filler and got ... this. Played just one game but I don't see too much tactics or strategy or, well, anything in it. It  looks like there are always obvious moves that are luck-triggered and at the end you are likely to get a draw anyhow.   Sold it.

[Rating: 3/10] B218 is a quick WW2 game that mimics supply line management whilst protecting your base and attacking your opponents. The game is good for what it is but sadly I find little interest in the theme or the implementation of the mechanics.   I would recommend this to WW2 folks who want something quick and light that they can play with a buddy who won't play one of those long, deep war games they have sitting lonely on the shelf.   UPDATE:  Gave it as a gift to Josiah (turned 9).

[Rating: 3/10] I like the theory of combining support, fire, and supplies in a spatial tile-driven combat.  In practice, the game is a repetitive slog that goes back and forth, offers little chance for cleverness, and overstays its welcome.  Mostly it's a stalemate, and you only make progress when somebody gets a poor draw.  More than anything else, it's boring.

[Rating: 3.5/10] Felt unforgiving for a beginner and after the opponent had some built up some units, I felt it was a lost cause.

[Rating: 4/10] Rating based on plays with computer version. Feels too abstract, relies heavily on card counting, and left me quite cold.

[Rating: 4/10] I really don't see the point in this one.  There are a lot of other two player games I'd rather play than this one.
